I'm not an Idiopathic hypersomniac, and couldn't possibly know what you're going through, but I used to feel really tired during the day.

I found that my problem was rooted in nutrition.

  • Try setting constant meal times, eat at a particular hour during the day and make it a habit.

  • Breakfast is also very important. Consider that you didn't eat for over 8 hours (or more, depending on if what you ate last night could even quality as food), your body is tired, and you're going to really feel it during the day (at around 1pm) if you didn't eat all this time.

One more thing to consider, are you fat? Are you eating right? Being overweight because of a poor diet can lead to fatigue. A high intake of fast food or junk food, refined sugars found in carbonated beverages, candy and processed snacks, and white flour results in higher fat storage in your body and a deficiency of vital nutrients.

Try exercising during the day (at least 30 minutes a day), and get enough water (1.5 liters, especially during summertime). Sleep experts recommend 30 minutes of exposure to sunlight a day because daylight helps regulate our sleep patterns.
